subject: Activation window carve-in proposal for APAC warm standby
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@finco.io>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@finco.io
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: APAC activation window carve-in for warm standby

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are reviewing Redwood for primary inference across our payments stack. Two quick asks that matter to our regulators in APAC:

1) Our compliance team wants clarity on when Redwood considers a regional switchover "activated" for SLA purposes. For regulatory reporting we need a defined RTO that starts when our systems are live on the standby region, not when a background sync completes.
2) Because of network peering differences in APAC, we may need a temporary carve-in to the activation window (i.e., a longer allowable lead time before SLA uptime/latency commitments begin) while we validate the warm-standby connectivity.

Can Redwood do a temporary carve-in for APAC (90 days) that shifts the SLA start to 30 minutes after our acceptance tests pass, and provide a signed addendum? That would let us run pilots while we finish peering and KMS alignment.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of whether this is doable and what info you need from us.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Infra Risk — FinCo Payments

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@finco.io>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, contracts@finco.io
Date: Thu, 3 Apr 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: APAC activation window carve-in for warm standby

Hi Lena —

Thanks — great question and totally reasonable for a pilot. High-level answer: yes, we can agree to a temporary carve-in that defines the SLA "activation" moment as 30 minutes after you confirm acceptance tests (AT) complete, for a fixed 90-day pilot.

Quick notes:
- This would be an exception to our standard standby activation policy; we need internal alignment on liability and monitoring hooks.
- We will require the AT checklist and a short runbook that shows how you will validate traffic and KV cache priming.
- During the carve-in period we propose a slightly different uptime target for APAC: 99.5% (monthly) rather than our standard 99.9% until peering is validated.

I'm looping in Naomi (Customer Reliability) for operational acceptance criteria and Karthik (SLA/legal owner) for contract language and liability. Aditya is CC'd for visibility on the engineering risk.

If that approach is acceptable I'll ask Contracts to draft an addendum and Operations to produce a temporary runbook template. Can you share the acceptance checklist and the expected pilot start date?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, Lena Ortiz <lena@finco.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Apr 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: APAC activation window carve-in for warm standby

Lena / Priya —

Operational confirm: we can support an acceptance-driven activation and the 30-minute buffer. For the pilot (90 days) we'll require:

- An acceptance checklist covering: synthetic traffic validation, keyspace priming confirmation, KMS access test, and a DNS/peering smoke test.
- A daily health snapshot (first 14 days) and then weekly until the carve-in is removed.
- Runbook attachment: we will provide a warm-standby-runbook template and expect FinCo to fill the sections under "customer validation steps".

Regarding metrics and SLOs: during the carve-in we will run with a 99.5% monthly uptime SLA for APAC and a per-request p50/p95 latency objective rather than guaranteed p99 latency SLA. That gives us room to tune batching and KV cache priming for your traffic shape.

I'll attach the runbook and a short MAP (mutual action plan) outlining responsibilities.

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Reliability & Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: warm-standby-runbook.docx

From: contracts@redwood.com
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@finco.io>, priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2025 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: Proposed SLA addendum (FinCo pilot)

Lena / Priya —

Attached is a draft addendum: proposed_sla_addendum.pdf. Key points summarized here:

1) Scope: Temporary carve-in for APAC warm-standby activation only; pilot term = 90 days from the mutually agreed start date.
2) Activation definition: SLA counting starts 30 minutes after FinCo provides a signed acceptance confirmation and after Redwood receives the completed acceptance checklist.
3) SLA targets for pilot: 99.5% monthly uptime (APAC region) and latency objectives (p50/p95) per the attached table.
4) Liability: Standard limited remedy applies; credits for downtime during the carve-in period are pro-rated using the 99.5% baseline.
5) Termination: Either party may terminate the pilot with 7 days' notice; upon termination standard SLA terms resume immediately if the region is fully validated.

Please review and flag any redlines. Karthik will lead the final negotiation if there are material changes.

Regards,
Contracts Team — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_sla_addendum.pdf

From: Lena Ortiz <lena@finco.io>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, contracts@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Apr 2025 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Proposed SLA addendum (FinCo pilot)

Thanks everyone — this is very clear and close to what we need. A couple of small asks before we sign:

- Can we add an explicit acceptance signature field and timestamp in the addendum (so there's no later dispute about when the 30-minute clock starts)?
- For the first 14 days, can Redwood agree to 15-minute webhook health alerts in addition to daily snapshots? That helps our on-call rotate with minimal blind spots.

If you can include those two items I can push for sign-off from our legal and infra risk teams today.

Best,
Lena
